title: Ringed-topos morphism and its induced module direct image
statement: For small sites $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ in the chosen universe [def-weil-size-convention] and sheaves of rings $A,B$, a ringed-topos morphism from $(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),A)$ to $(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),B)$ consists of an adjunction $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ on sheaves of sets, with $f^{-1}$ preserving finite limits, and a morphism of ring objects $f^{-1}B\to A$. Equip it with its induced additive direct image on module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]: its underlying sheaf is naturally $f_*$ of the underlying sheaf, its addition is the induced addition, and its $B$-action is the one induced by the structural ring map. Equivalently, under the sheaf adjunction, generalized module elements satisfy $\widetilde{a x+y}=f^\sharp(f^{-1}a)\widetilde x+\widetilde y$. The structural map preserves $0,1,+,\cdot$ on generalized elements, with inverse-image products identified by finite-limit preservation. The displayed identifications are natural in the module. This is a geometric morphism of the sheaf topoi, with no requirement that it be induced by a functor between the presented sites.
